cosmology.architects_are: Exactly twenty-two members of a dissident Thay’lmériûn sect who presented themselves as gods on Universal.
cosmology.original_planet: A desolate, predominantly lava-based planet before terraforming.
cosmology.terraforming: The sect transformed a predominantly lava-based world into a dense greenhouse planet through twenty-two exclusive environmental mandates.
cosmology.class_manipulation: The twenty-two class channels were deliberately tuned to the sect members’ claimed divine identities so power manifestation would reinforce their cults.
cosmology.era_invariance: All twenty-two classes and all six path families are available in every era and location; expression and equipment change, not class identity.
cosmology.sect_motive: They rejected the cultivated and synthetic food sources used by much of Thay’lmériûn civilization.
cosmology.theft: They stole experimental genetic code and terraforming technology.
cosmology.origin_context: The Twenty-Two are one predatory sect within the larger Thay’lmériûn civilization. This edition includes all 34 Universal homeworld peoples and all 26 preserved Alien-Folk profiles present in the attached concordance.
cosmology.terraforming_assignment_rule: Every listed biome variant has exactly one responsible Architect; every Architect has at least one assignment; overlap is prohibited.
cosmology.genome_program_scope: The Universal homeworld peoples are included as populations shaped by or descended from the stolen genetic program. The Alien-Folk are independent off-world peoples. Public race-to-deity associations describe religion and culture rather than compulsory worship or sole biological ownership.

Their animal expression never overrides personhood or communal duty, which connects kinship obligations to Nebyrr’s social order.

Their legal recognition as persons and communal stewardship of memory are tied to civilization and social order.
Encoding law and civic agreements in song connects the Cliffsong Folk to ordered civilization.
